post.caption:
Light enters a raindrop, refracts, reflects off the back and refracts again on the way out, with each colour bending slightly differently. It all emerges at about 42 degrees from your line of sight, which means a rainbow is a circle centred on your own shadow. From the ground the horizon cuts off the bottom half; from an aircraft you can see the whole ring. And nobody sees yours, because their circle is built from different droplets entirely.
